importance_ranking.reason: Significant visual sub-type variation exists between walk-in control room cabins, skid-mounted units, and portable cabins — buyers use the image to confirm product type before reading any text. The critical wrong-product risk (cabin vs panel enclosure/cabinet) is resolved at the image stage; wrong type is an immediate skip.

Panel Type, Protection Class, Material, and Mounting are non-interchangeable shortlisting gates — an APFC cabin cannot substitute for a PLC control room, and an IP42 indoor cabin cannot substitute for an IP65 outdoor installation. Buyers arrive with a project-specific requirement and use specs to confirm fit before any contact.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant recognised brand names exist in the Indian control panel cabin market — it is served by fragmented regional fabricators and buyers search by fabricator capability and spec, not brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: Custom fabrication with post-sale dependency (site delivery, installation support, commissioning) means buyers evaluate fabricator track record, certifications, and project execution capability during vendor selection. Institutional and government buyers conduct vendor qualification before awarding orders.

Every cabin is custom-fabricated to project-specific dimensions and fittings — no fixed unit price exists and final price is always negotiated. Listed price serves as a budget entry point for Indian buyers after spec and company qualification; India price sensitivity applies but price comparison across listings is only meaningful after spec equivalence is confirmed.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Per piece is the dominant and universally understood unit for discrete cabin structures. A minority sub-segment of large modular control rooms is quoted per sq ft of floor area, but this is not the primary buyer expectation and does not create meaningful price comparison confusion at the listing tile level.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is entirely implied for a discrete prefabricated structure — no buyer questions whether a control panel cabin is sold per piece. The per sq ft sub-segment exception is captured in unit_note but does not warrant showing unit on all listings.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines what electrical equipment the cabin houses — APFC vs MCC vs HT Panel vs PLC are non-interchangeable product classes with fundamentally different internal layouts, busbar sizing, and ventilation requirements, producing large price deltas across values.

IP42 (indoor) vs IP65/IP66 (outdoor, dust and water-tight) represents a significant price delta driven by sealed cable glands, gaskets, and robust construction — buyers cannot substitute a lower IP class for outdoor installations, making this a hard shortlisting gate.

missing_important_specs.why_important: PUF sandwich panel insulation vs non-insulated MS sheet construction is a primary price and performance differentiator for outdoor and hot-climate installations — buyers specify insulation requirement upfront and sellers need it to confirm construction method and quote accurately.

AC provision is a major cost adder and a common mandatory requirement for PLC/SCADA control rooms in hot climates — sellers need this to determine whether to include AC unit supply and installation in their quote.

Control Panel Cabins are custom-fabricated to buyer-specified floor area and height — sellers need dimensional requirements to assess fabrication feasibility, material quantity, and project cost before responding.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Steel vs FRP defines the structural and environmental suitability of the cabin — FRP is required for corrosive or coastal environments where steel would corrode, and sellers need this to confirm they can supply the specified construction type.

missing_important_specs.why_important: The type of electrical equipment to be housed (APFC, MCC, PLC, VFD, HT) determines the entire cabin configuration — internal layout, busbar sizing, ventilation, and dimensions — and sellers cannot quote accurately without this information.
IP rating defines whether the cabin is for indoor or outdoor installation — sellers need this to confirm construction method, sealing requirements, and material grade before responding to the RFQ.

Whether the buyer needs PUF insulation or a non-insulated structure determines construction method and cost — sellers need this to provide an accurate quote for outdoor or temperature-sensitive installations.
